items.body: Slice 1 of #6032 (design #6031). This lands the **pure decision layer** of the generic browser-dependent quota watchdog — the part the issue calls out as the natural fit for PBT/MBT — and leaves the I/O, browser and deployment shell to a follow-up with the boundary written down. ## What lands `pm-stack/exporters/src/watchdog-state.ts` - **Failure classes** — `session-expired`, `cookie-missing`, `endpoint-changed`, `browser-down`, `cdp-unreachable`, `rate-limited`, `unknown`, and the single place a class maps to a repair rung. - **Repair ladder** — `decide()` returns the next action (`quiet`, `wait-cooldown`, `retry`, `repair rung N`, `human-blocked`, `escalate`) plus the next persisted record. Per-rung attempts are capped at 2 per incident; a rate-limited source sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and the next tick honors it with no browser action; a rate limit whose cooldown rung is spent escalates rather than climbing to a browser repair. - **Disk state** — `SourceHealth` carries `lastAttemptAt`, `lastSuccessAt`, `consecutiveFailures`, `currentClass`, sanitized `lastDetail`, `cooldownUntil`, per-rung `rungAttempts`, a bounded (20) `repairLog`, and the incident identity + surfacing flag. `coerceHealth` reads a file back without trusting it: garbage yields a fresh record, never a throw and never an assumed-healthy. - **Sanitization** — credential-shaped text is redacted before it can reach the state file or a log. No I/O, no browser, no secrets, no provider names — the core is provider-agnostic by construction, which is what the adapter-loader criterion asks for. ## Tests name their oracles `pm-stack/exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts` — **12 pass, 0 fail**: - **PBT invariants** over generated tick sequences: per-rung attempts never exceed the cap; the repair log stays bounded; `consecutiveFailures` is monotonic while failing and resets on success; a healthy tick always clears the incident and is quiet; no secret-shaped value survives sanitization. - **MBT** — a reference model of the ladder written independently of the implementation, stepped in lockstep over 300 generated sequences; any divergence in action, rung, or failure count fails. - **Acceptance fixtures**: the broken-source walk (retry → CDP re-validation → re-login → escalation), the rate-limited cooldown persisted and honored then escalating, the human-only challenge marking the incident `human-blocked` with the surfacing flag and not re-hammering, and the healthy source staying quiet. ```bash cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test ../exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts ``` Typecheck of both new files is clean under the repo's strict settings. ## What remains for #6032 (listed in `pm-stack/exporters/README.md`) The oneshot entry point (state read/write, `latest.json` + heartbeat reads, history append), the adapter loader and `adapters/`, the rung 2/3 executors, the rung-4 hand-off to #6033, producer scaffolding, and the systemd oneshot + timer. The issue stays open for those. Refs #6032, #6031. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(pm-stack): quota watchdog core — entry point, adapters, rung executors, systemd timer (#6032)
items.body: ## What this builds (#6032 remainder) Slice 1 (decision layer, PR #7788) and rung 4 (escalation, PR #8357) already landed. This PR builds the rest of the watchdog core: - **`src/watchdog.ts`** — the oneshot entry point. Per tick: load adapters, read the state file through `coerceHealth`, observe each source (producer document + gatherer heartbeat + live CDP liveness probe), classify (including missing-document, stale-read-while-the-browser-lives, and dead-CDP — the classes the producer cannot see itself), `decide`, execute the rung, run rung-4 escalation/recovery, write state back atomically (tmp+rename), append `quota-watchdog-history.jsonl`. Nothing decision-relevant lives in process memory (#5928). - **Rung executors** — rung 2: CDP re-validation (`/json/version` + `/json/list`, allowlist origin open, cookies present **by name** via the CDP websocket — values never enter the process) with one bounded supervised restart of the adapter's browser unit; rung 3: re-login driver that stops dead at a human-only challenge and marks the incident human-blocked. Repairs are gated on `QUOTA_WATCHDOG_LIVE_REPAIRS=1`, rung-4 production effectors (fleet queue / `gh`) on `QUOTA_WATCHDOG_LIVE=1`; the systemd unit sets both, a bare CLI run journals dry-run plans and creates nothing. - **`src/adapters.ts` + `adapters/fixture.json`** — the adapter loader: per-provider JSON (origins allowlist, CDP port, data paths, cookie names, login hints, class/rung maps, thresholds), structurally validated, defects reported per file instead of throwing. The core contains zero provider names; the fixture adapter is the one shipped here, real provider adapters are follow-ons per the issue scope. - **`producers/producer-template.mjs`** — forkable producer scaffold from the retired Meta producer pattern (timeout-bounded CDP, tab ownership, failure-class exit codes + failure documents, atomic `latest.json`), plus `test/fixtures/fixture-producer.mjs`, the scenario-driven stub the acceptance tests drive. - **`pm-stack/systemd/pm-quota-watchdog.{service,timer}`** — oneshot + timer on the gatherer cadence, offset to `*:3/15`. ## Tests (oracles named per the testing doctrine) `bun test ../exporters/test/` — **35 pass, 0 fail** (includes the pre-existing state + escalation suites). The new `test/watchdog.test.ts` drives the entry point end to end against a scratch tree: - broken source walks retry → CDP re-validation → re-login → escalation, caps honored (no rung >2× per incident), escalates exactly once and dedupes on later ticks; - rate-limited fixture sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and a fresh tick honors it with no repair action (the #5928 regression shape); - human-only challenge fixture marks the incident human-blocked with the surfacing flag and a same-tick NEEDS DREW line, and the ladder stops dead; - healthy source is quiet (state + history only, no output); - recovery after escalation comments/closes/completes the hand-off; - cross-invocation persistence: every tick re-reads state from disk. CLI fixture demo also run live: healthy tick quiet; `session-expired` scenario classified and rung 3 recorded (as `skipped` with live repairs off). Live install (units + timer + a laptop-local adapter for the Meta file-export source) and the ≥3-consecutive-tick demonstration follow the merge and are reported on #6032. items.title: fix(message-bridge): sign in with OAuth on the bare address
items.body: Before: Claude's Message Bridge connector is set to `https://bridge.security.cab` with no token in the path. Every call from Claude got a 404 (Cloudflare logs show only `/`, `/.well-known/*` and `/register` requests from Claude), so the tools showed up and then dropped. After: the bare address (`/` and `/mcp`) is the same MCP server behind OAuth 2.1. Claude registers itself, Drew approves on the bridge's own page (one tap in a browser that has opened the history page, otherwise paste the page link), and Claude refreshes its token on its own. The `/mcp/` URLs keep working with no sign-in. How: new `src/oauth.js` adds protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, dynamic client registration, `/authorize` (PKCE S256 only, same-origin posts, CSP `form-action` limited to the client's redirect origin) and `/token` (code and refresh grants, public or secret clients). Nothing is stored: client ids, codes and tokens are HMAC-signed with a key derived from `ACCESS_TOKEN`, so rotating that token revokes every grant. Opening `/p/` sets a `__Host-` owner cookie (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax). The ChatGPT token approves ChatGPT's channel only. 7 new tests (34 pass); README updated. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added OAuth sign-in for the bridge, including client registration, authorization, token exchange, refresh, and approval. * Enabled bearer-authenticated MCP access at the bridge’s root and `/mcp` addresses. * Added channel-specific access: bridge credentials grant Claude access, while ChatGPT credentials grant access only through ChatGPT. * Added an owner-only OAuth event log for troubleshooting. * **Bug Fixes** * Rotating an access token revokes existing OAuth grants; reusing an older refresh token revokes its token family. * **Documentation** * Updated setup guidance for OAuth and token-based connections, token lifetimes, approval, and supported access routes.

items.title: feat(mcpx): opencode v2 plugin core — {id, setup}, namespaced tools, ctx.storage (#1858)
items.body:
Completes the core rewrite for #1858, following the verified map in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/opencode-plugin-v2.md` §6 (groundwork PR #2457, merged). Related: #730 (the fleet's deployed `.opencode/plugin/` copy — a different artifact; this core's shape is what gets ported there under #730, not in this PR).

**The v2 tree** (`pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/`, beside the untouched v1 files):
- `index.ts` — `export default { id: "mcpx", setup }`; setup wires storage warm-read, context hook, session-env, timing, and tool registration last (registration can never fail setup)
- `options.ts` — v1 `Options` + resolution for every setting the core consumes, property reads of declared names only (settings guard)
- `session-env.ts` — `PUT /api/session/:id/environment` once per session with the **full** env (route replaces; doc §3), quiet degrade with no `serverUrl`
- `context.ts` — idempotent system-prompt paragraph via `session.hook("context")`
- `remember.ts` — remembered daemon on `ctx.storage`, until-gone via health-check drop; no state file
- `timing.ts` — `execute.after` records for both statuses of the union (failures recorded, not just successes)
- `tools.ts` — `tool.transform` registration under the `mcpx` namespace: `discover` / `exec` / `observe` plus `daemon_status` / `daemon_select` / `daemon_forget`, gated exactly as v1 (tools opt-in; daemon tools when asked, when the full set is on, or when boot discovery is ambiguous). Verified against the pin: `editor.namespace({ name, description })`, plain JSON Schema inputs, and `effectiveName` flattening means the model still sees `mcpx_exec` etc. §7's namespace question is resolved in the doc.
- `daemon.ts` — re-export of the shared harness-free daemon core (socket-first per #53/#44, reused not rewritten)

**Honest v2 differences** (recorded in tools.ts): the v2 ToolContext has no `ctx.ask`, so `daemon_select` applies the choice directly instead of confirming; there is no TUI channel in the server context slice, so ambiguity rides the tool-result annotation line rather than toasts.

**NOT in this PR — the SET-REMAINDER on #1858**, to be enqueued when this core lands: sampling answers via `ctx.generate.text`, `mcp.transform` filtered per-session registration, `permission.hook("evaluate")`, and the promise-based TUI `select()` daemon picker. Server-side `_meta['ai.opencode/sessionID']` attribution is #1932's tracked work, not this PR.

**Tests:** `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — 15 pass (context/storage/session-env + the new tools.test.ts: registration names, gating, executor fallbacks, storage-backed select scopes); full plugin suite 50 tests, 0 fail, on the laptop worktree. Go settings guards (`TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting`, script-env) run in CI over the new tree.
